analysis: The method checkMtlsHoKToken is part of an OAuth2 token issuance process. It checks if MTLS HoK token binding is enabled for the client. If enabled, it attempts to bind the access token (and optionally the refresh token) with a client certificate from the request/session. If the certificate binding results in null (i.e., no valid certificate is available), the method logs an error and throws a CorsErrorResponseException. This exception is a runtime exception that carries explicit error details (CORS context, OAuth error code, message, HTTP status). The method does not declare a throws clause, so callers are not forced to catch it. However, in typical web application frameworks, such exceptions are intended to be caught by a global exception handler or an error mapping layer that converts them into appropriate HTTP error responses. The exception's name and structure strongly suggest it is designed for that purpose. The throw occurs only in the else branch when a required certificate is missing, which is a client error (bad request). Thus, the programmer likely expects that the exception will propagate to an external handler that will generate a proper error response to the client, not that it will be ignored or cause an unhandled crash.
